label: At D1 drops after rare a1->S2, rises after rare a2->S1; at GO falls with S1 belief.
terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 1) * (prev_state == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_state == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * belief_lo ;; (phase == GO) * last_is("a1 S1 r") ;; (phase == GO) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * (tv("reward", -2) == 1)
explanation: Update gate z of unit 17 is near 1 (mostly at D2, where it barely varies). Its magnitude beyond timing mostly comes from the last trial transition at D1: z drops sharply (about -0.21) at D1 after an a1 choice that rare-transitioned to S2, regardless of reward, and rises (+0.085) after a rare a2->S1 transition. Common transitions leave it near baseline. At GO it falls graded with the ideal-observer log-odds that S1 is good (higher when S2 is favoured). Reward on the last trial matters little. The free fit adds a GO dip after a1 S1 rewarded, a GO rise after a2 choices, and a D1 term for reward two trials back (dev 0.635 vs 0.572 short). Some large unexplained D1 drops remain in single windows. Uses only observed variables.

issues: The claims check out against the profile residuals. At D1 after a1 S2 the residual is -0.206 when rewarded and -0.203 when not, so reward makes no difference. After a2 S1 it is +0.083 (r) and +0.094 (u). At GO the residual falls steadily across belief deciles, from +0.057 to -0.078. At D2 it stays within about 0.01.

Each term is needed. Dropping the GO belief_lo term cuts test R^2 from 0.550 to 0.364. Dropping the D1 a2->S1 term cuts it to 0.491. Using raw belief instead of belief_lo gives 0.463, and widening belief_lo to D1 as well (phase != D2) gives 0.464. So the GO-only, log-odds form is correct.

'Common transitions leave it near baseline' is only roughly true. After a1 S1 the D1 residual is about +0.04. Replacing the D1 a2->S1 term with D1*(prev_state==1) ('raised after reaching S1') does slightly better: test 0.563 vs 0.550, dev 0.586 vs 0.572. The two labels say nearly the same thing.

There is a large non-systematic miss class. Many worst-fit windows show D1 drops of about 0.35-0.4 after common a2->S2 trials (often an a2 trial that followed an a1 trial), and the short form predicts baseline there. Averaged over each previous-trial cell these errors are small: the largest systematic error is +0.06 (GO after a2 S2 u). Observed-only probes for them (two trials back, D1*belief_lo, a2-after-a1) each add only 0.01-0.035, so they stay unexplained. The explanation does admit this. The 'all observed' ceiling is 0.73 against 0.55-0.56 for the short form.
Adding the future upcoming choice at D1 (D1*(action==1)) raises R^2 only to about 0.59, so future variables are not needed.
